correctness.rationale: For the pure equality/E signature and nonempty finite models, a three-round Duplicator invariant proves every model is rank-three equivalent to one of 63 profiles. A complete finite recursively-defined first-order type signature partitions those profiles into exactly 21 groups, and an independently implemented two-sided EF minimax game verifies all 63 memberships and 210 separations. The representative orders are at most nine; two explicit rank-three sentences force three classes each of size at least three, proving a nine-point lower bound. All embedded checker paths were executed and their table matched. No unverified extrapolation from finite cases is used.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural rank-three classification over the elementary but genuinely binary equivalence signature, with a sharp universal smallest-model bound. The result is stronger than finite-rank finiteness and provides explicit canonical test instances for rank-bounded model comparison. Rank three is the first level at which triples in one class and triples of distinct classes both become visible. The exact 63-to-21 collapse and nine-point extremum are non-obvious and reproducible; no arbitrary graph slice or unsupported downstream theorem is invoked.
